title: What's new and what's next for Amazon ECS
abstract: Amazon ECS keeps getting simpler to run and more capable at scale. Product and engineering leadership view of where it is headed next. Recent investments make ECS faster to deploy applications, more cost-efficient, and ready for a new class of AI and agentic workloads. Discusses the range of compute options from Fargate to Amazon ECS Managed Instances and how they provide customers choice and flexibility. Learn how to apply the newest ECS capabilities today, and what to plan for as the roadmap unfolds. Bryan favorite: ECS evolution, AI/agentic workloads, compute flexibility.

title: Ambient accessibility: Architecting real-time ASL on a Wearable
abstract: What if a DHH person could wear a device and get sign language translation of every conversation around them in under a second? Architects a pipeline that ingests Amazon Bee's ambient audio, transcribes it, transforms English to ASL grammar, generates avatar animations, and streams signed video back. That one-second constraint drives every architectural tradeoff, from whether translation stages run on-device for speed or in the cloud for accuracy, to whether we sign full sentences or start mid-utterance with partial context. Explores the edge-cloud splits and pipeline staging that make sub-second delivery feasible. Bryan favorite: accessibility, ASL, avatar animation, edge-cloud latency splits, the sumerian-hosts / deaf-blind-narrative territory.
